title: Artifact lifecycle catalog and driver rollback playbooks for LTS channels
text:
Artifact lifecycle catalog and driver rollback playbooks for LTS channels

description:
Problem: We lack a single authoritative artifact lifecycle catalog that maps container images, SBOMs, and CUDA/driver pinsets to LTS channels and rollout gates. Operators currently rely on ad-hoc docs and per-release runbooks; this increases blast radius during upgrades and makes rollbacks error-prone.

Goal: Deliver an artifact lifecycle catalog and automated rollback playbooks for LTS channels that: 1) enumerate canonical image artifacts and their SBOMs; 2) map each artifact to compatible CUDA/driver stacks with tested compatibility metadata; 3) define deterministic promotion rules across staging -> canary -> production; 4) provide runnable rollback playbooks (k8s manifests + infra steps) with automated validation smoke tests.

Scope:
- Author a machine- and operator-readable catalog (YAML/JSON manifest per artifact) that includes image tag, sbom uri, build id, pinned cuda/driver version, expected kernel modules, and verification hash.
- Define promotion and gating rules: preflight checks, SLO smoke thresholds, canary % progression, automatic bail/rollback triggers.
- Implement rollback playbooks for the most common failure modes: model degradation, driver incompatibility, kernel panic on nodes, and image corruption. Playbooks should include the minimal steps to revert serving pools and rotate caches.
- Integrate with existing image promotion pipeline and the SBOM sync service so catalog entries are created/updated automatically on successful CI.
- Add a compatibility test matrix and two automated test suites: a fast smoke suite for gating and a longer regression suite run in staging.

Non-goals: Full multi-arch image build rework; we will reference existing build outputs. Golden image creation for on-prem appliances is out of scope for this ticket (covered in ENG-15323).

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Tighter pinning reduces unexpected regressions but increases upgrade friction; we will provide curated pin groups for customers who want faster upgrades.
- Automating rollbacks requires careful idempotency guarantees; we will limit automated rollbacks to well-tested scenarios and require human confirmation for major version downgrades.

Success criteria:
- Catalog contains entries for all images used by runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.21 LTS channels.
- A promoted canary that fails smoke tests triggers the rollback playbook in under 10 minutes during test runs.
- On-call runbook time-to-recover for driver-related incidents decreases by 40% in the next release window.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Catalog JSON/YAML artifacts generated automatically for each CI-built image and visible in the release-infra bucket. 2) Compatibility table populated for all artifacts used in runtime-1.20/1.21 LTS channels. 3) Runbook and a tested rollback-playbook that reverts a canary roll to the previous image and pinned driver with <10 min mean time for the automated scenario. 4) Automated gating integration with release pipeline (canary fail -> block promotion) and dashboards showing gate status.

comments:
2026-02-21 - Lina Chen: Drafted initial problem statement and scope. Linked upstream dependency list. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RELEASE/Artifact+Lifecycle+Catalog
2026-02-26 - Miguel Torres: Spike completed for catalog schema and example manifests. PR created: https://github.com/redwood/release-infra/pull/412 (schema + generator). Needs review from Security for SBOM URIs.
2026-03-02 - Aisha Kapoor (Security): Reviewed SBOM exposure model; recommended using signed SBOM URIs and short-lived GCS tokens. Filed follow-up ENG-15322 for tokenization work.
2026-03-05 - QA (Darian Patel): Ran smoke suite against promoted canary; false-positive due to missing GPU driver test. Added driver compatibility check to smoke gate (see PR 421).
2026-03-09 - Miguel Torres: Implemented rollback playbook prototype and tested rollback on staging cluster. Playbook execution log: https://logs.redwood.com/playbooks/ENG-15321/staging-run-20260309. Observed cache invalidation race on 2/10 nodes; added serialized cache rotate step.
2026-03-10 - Product (Rhea Singh): Approved promotion gating thresholds for LTS channels pending one more regression run.
